claim: Tan et al. (ICLR 2025) compares BO-qEI, CMA-ES, REINFORCE, and Gradient Ascent (plus mean/min ensemble variants) as optimizers against a roughly-fixed regression-based surrogate class, making it the closest one-axis optimizer sweep found in this audit, but it never tests a Gaussian process surrogate class and embeds the comparison inside a 22-method confounded leaderboard rather than a controlled 2-factor design.
stance_target: N6: a crossed surrogate x optimizer factorial in offline MBO already exists in prior work
scope_conditions: Design-Bench, 5 tasks (Ant, D'Kitty, Superconductor, TF-Bind-8, TF-Bind-10), ICLR 2025
quoted_support: The first category involves baselines that optimize a trained regression-based model, such as BO-qEI (Garnett, 2023; Shahriari et al., 2016), CMA-ES (Hansen, 2016), REINFORCE (Williams, 1992), Gradient Ascent and its variants of mean ensemble and min ensemble.

claim: Grepping Tan et al.'s full text for factorial/ANOVA/crossed/two-way/variance-decomposition terminology returns zero hits, confirming no statistical variance decomposition between surrogate-class and optimizer-class effects is computed anywhere in the paper.
stance_target: N6: Tan et al. runs a two-way ANOVA or equivalent variance decomposition

claim: Tan et al. finds only weak correlation (Spearman 0.23 on D'Kitty, -0.24 on TF-Bind-8) between a surrogate's out-of-distribution MSE and the final optimization score obtained via gradient ascent on that surrogate, arguing MSE is a poor proxy for surrogate quality in offline MBO.
stance_target: surrogate evaluation methodology in offline MBO
scope_conditions: D'Kitty (continuous) and TF-Bind-8 (discrete) Design-Bench tasks, 5 surrogate variants, 8 seeds
